source.title: SLlama: Parameter-Efficient Language Model Architecture for Enhanced Linguistic Competence Under Strict Data Constraints
source.authors: V. Omolaoye; B. Owoyele; Gerard de Melo

record.file_problem: None; the full paper, including appendices and tables, is present.
record.tranche_reason: The paper does not measure held-out cross-entropy or fit scaling laws. It does sweep model configurations and report downstream benchmark results and scale-performance associations, bearing on V6 by a different measure.
record.gate_note: The paper cites Hoffmann et al. and uses a 1:2 parameter-to-token heuristic to motivate a roughly 5M-parameter target, but it does not test that compute-optimal allocation. It reports no held-out pretraining cross-entropy, scaling-law fit, or extrapolation. The 24-configuration sweep in Table 4 and its reported trends are relevant to V6. Table 2's component comparisons do not test the claim versions.
record.test_reason: Appendix A sweeps 24 tied-embedding Llama configurations (hidden size 64–1,024, 2–10 layers). All are trained on the same 10M-token BabyLM data for 3,000 iterations. The authors report how model size relates to downstream BLiMP, GLUE and EWoK scores. This is a new, data-bottlenecked, tiny-model setting with a result on V6. No pretraining loss, fits or allocation sweeps are reported, so V1–V5 and V7 are not tested.
record.authors_conclusion: The record over-weights the appendix sweep. The authors' main conclusion is different: embedding weight tying degrades linguistic competence in small models. They also conclude that a compact untied architecture, SLlama (2.6M parameters), beats larger baselines such as Baby Llama (58M) by 31.72% on BLiMP under a 10M-token budget. The sweep finding is secondary: only weak correlations between size and scores, with more data needed to confirm them.
record.recipe_differences: A data-constrained architecture/configuration sweep with downstream benchmark evaluation, not a held-out cross-entropy scaling-law fit or compute-optimal allocation study.
record.method_sensitivity: Reported downstream associations differ by configuration dimension and task: hidden size has a weak consistent positive association with BLiMP, an inconsistent positive relationship with GLUE, and a strong consistent negative correlation with world knowledge; layer count has weak trends that differ between linguistic competence and conceptual understanding.
record.peer_reviewed: Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing (EMNLP 2025)
record.problems: The scaling-related evidence is limited to a 24-configuration sweep on the Llama architecture under a 10M-token data constraint. The paper says statistical significance was generally weak and that more data is needed; it reports no uncertainty intervals for the table scores and no pretraining-loss measurements.
record.rows_left_out: Table 4's BLiMP supplement and EWoK scores for all 24 configurations are not extracted as individual rows because the 60-row cap was reached after retaining BLiMP and GLUE scores and the aggregate trends most directly relevant to V6. The paper's figure caption gives Spearman correlations of 0.38 and 0.88 but does not unambiguously map each value to a particular comparison in the supplied text; they are not assigned to rows.

untested.parts: Relation of downstream performance to pretraining loss; any setting where data is not the bottleneck; models larger than about 120M parameters; parameter counts per configuration are not reported.

missing.what: Strong, consistent negative correlation between hidden size and world knowledge (EWoK); a reversed downstream scale trend.
missing.locator: Appendix A, Characterizing the Llama Architecture, trend 3; Table 4 EWoK column

missing.what: Spearman correlations of 0.38 and 0.88 for hidden size/layers versus BLiMP/GLUE. The mapping of each value to a comparison is ambiguous.
Tied models: 2.4M scores 56.0% BLiMP and 120M scores 64.5% BLiMP under the same 10M tokens; a modest gain with roughly 50x the parameters.

record.verdict_notes: The record's 'challenges' label is too strong. Every sweep model has the same fixed 10M-token budget, a regime where scaling laws themselves expect parameter gains to saturate. Comparisons with Llama-3.2-3B and Baby Llama are cross-recipe and do not test scaling.

versions.untested_parts: No held-out pretraining loss is measured against parameters, tokens, or compute.
No fitted power law or prediction of larger-run loss is reported.
The 1:2 parameter-to-token heuristic is cited and used to choose a target size, but no fixed-compute allocation sweep or optimal split is measured.
The configuration sweep varies hidden size and layer count, but does not compare architecture details at a fixed parameter count using loss.
No other modality, repeated-data regime, fine-tuning, or transfer power-law test is reported.
No pretraining-loss-to-downstream-performance relation is tested; results are limited to the reported model configurations and downstream benchmarks.
No exponents or compute-optimal splits are fitted or compared across fitting methods, data, parameter-counting schemes, or training schedules.

relationships.condition: Tiny tied-embedding Llama models (hidden 64–1,024, 2–10 layers), all trained on the same 10M BabyLM tokens
relationships.reason: The macro-average score is not directly related to size (T4-49). Hidden size correlates only weakly or inconsistently with BLiMP and GLUE (T4-50, T4-51). Layer trends are weak and mixed in sign (T4-52, T4-53). Significance is weak, and data is fixed, so this regime is data-bottlenecked.
relationships.display_finding: Average performance had no direct relationship with model size, while hidden-width and depth relationships with BLiMP and GLUE were weak or inconsistent.

relation.reason: Its own configuration sweep directly examines relationships between model dimensions and downstream benchmark performance, bearing on V6.

tranche.reason: The architecture sweep reports downstream scaling results in a new setting of small tied-embedding models under a fixed, limited dataset.

source_check.notes: Appendix A mistakenly refers to Table 1 when discussing the Table 4 sweep and reports conflicting layer–linguistic-competence trends. The 10M tokens describe the dataset constraint; training lasted 3,000 iterations, so this is not a statement of total consumed tokens.

statements.correction: 24 tied-embedding Llama configurations; fixed 10M-token BabyLM dataset; no direct model-size–macro-score relationship; weak positive hidden-size–BLiMP association; inconsistent positive hidden-size–GLUE association; mixed layer trends; generally weak statistical significance; V6 verdict: limits_scope.
statements.problem: The description of this study is accurate, but its placement under challenges overstates the mixed, weak findings from this condition group.
